subject: Microburst coverage request + discount path for ShelfApp launch
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@shelfapp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Sep 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Short window headroom for launch week — need options

Hi Marissa,

Quick note from product: our QA load testing showed a ~6x spike for 72 hours during the new feature launch (expected 09/20–09/22). We need a temporary throughput buffer and clarity on overrun costs — preferably a single-line option we can show procurement.

Constraints:
- 72 hour window, start-of-day PST 09/20;
- Budget wants predictable cap on overrun exposure (they asked for an absolute $ cap);
- We may sign a 6‑month ramp commit if the trial goes well.

Can you outline the path: short-term headroom, per-token overrun rate, and any one-time administrative fees? Also, are there any onboarding quotas or SLA exceptions required to support the spike?

Thanks — Alyssa
Alyssa Chen
Head of Product, ShelfApp
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@shelfapp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Sep 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Short window headroom for launch week — need options

Alyssa —

Thanks for the heads up. Short answers up front: yes, we can provide a 72‑hour microburst pool and we offer two pricing tracks depending on risk appetite. I've looped in Ben and Karthik for pricing + operational coverage.

Quick clarifying Qs so we can put an accurate number in front of Procurement:
- Expected average token/sec over baseline during spike? (even a 95th percentile helps)
- Is ShelfApp able to accept an explicit dollar cap that applies to overrun only, or do you want blended prorated commit + cap?
- Any data residency/SOC scope for this short window (should be standard for hosted but wanted to confirm)?

If you prefer, Ben can send a succinct one‑pager for Procurement with a single recommended option.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@shelfapp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Sep 2027 13:18:00 -0700
Subject: Microburst pricing options (one‑page)

Alyssa —

Appended a short options summary below; I've also attached a detailed pricing workbook (microburst-pricing-sheet.xlsx). Pick the letter that maps to your risk profile and I will generate a concise procurement note.

Option A — Guarded Cap (recommended for Procurement)
- 72‑hour temporary headroom pool: 2.5M tokens total;
- Overrun protection: if usage exceeds 2.5M, automatic fallback to standard pay‑as‑you‑go at $0.0025 per token up to a hard $10k overrun cap;
- One‑time admin fee: $750 to enable the microburst policy and SLA exception;
- No required minimum commit; 30% discount off standard PAYG if you convert to a 3‑month minimum within 30 days.

Option B — Prorated Commit + Lower Overage
- Create a pro‑rated 1‑month commit covering anticipated spike (1.8M tokens) billed at the committed rate with 40% discount;
- Overrun above the commit charged at $0.0018 per token (lower), with no hard cap (recommended only if Procurement accepts variable exposure);
- Waived admin fee if you sign the prorated commit by 09/15.

Option C — Enterprise Safety Net (for committed accounts)
- 72‑hour headroom pooled on dedicated capacity with guaranteed throughput and $0 overrun for the first 2M tokens;
- Requires 6‑month commit;
- Price by quote — includes SLA uplift and white‑glove oncall.

Operational notes:
- We can flip Option A into B within 14 days if you provide a PO and convert to a short commit;
- No changes to data residency for hosted customers; standard SOC2 scope applies;
- Attachment: microburst-pricing-sheet.xlsx (breaks down per-token math and per-hour burn scenarios).

If Procurement wants a single signed doc, I can issue a one‑page amendment that mirrors Option A (guarded cap) and includes the hard dollar cap they requested.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Sales — Redwood Inference
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@shelfapp.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@shelfapp.com
Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Microburst pricing options (one‑page)

Ben/Marissa —

Thanks, this is helpful. Procurement is pushing for the simplest ask: a single amendment with a $9,500 hard cap on overrun, admin fee accepted. They also want confirmation the cap only applies to the 72‑hour window and that standard usage outside that window is billed normally. Two quick clarifications: 1) does the $9.5k cap include the admin fee or is that outside the cap? 2) If we hit the cap only on day 2, will you throttle or continue serving until the cap is reached?

If we can get those answers in writing we can route to procurement and (likely) sign the amendment.

—Alyssa
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@shelfapp.com>, procurement@shelfapp.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Sep 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Microburst pricing options (one‑page)

Alyssa/Procurement —

Confirming in writing per your questions:
- The $9,500 hard cap applies to overrun spend only; the $750 admin fee is invoiced separately and is not counted toward the $9.5k cap.
- We will not throttle mid‑window by default. If the hard cap is reached, the configured behavior is: 1) send automated alerts at 75% and 90% of the cap; 2) once the cap hits $9,500 we will either (a) pause serving (if you select the capped protection behavior) or (b) allow continued serving and bill at the standard PAYG rate. For the amendment we will include the default to pause serving upon cap hit; you may opt to allow continued serving by initialing Section 2 of the amendment.

Next steps: Ben will draft a one‑page amendment that mirrors Option A with the $9,500 overrun cap and the $750 admin fee outside the cap. If Procurement confirms they want the default pause behavior we will send a DocuSign link (signature-request-link.url).

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments referenced: microburst-pricing-sheet.xlsx, shelfapp-mop-draft.docx
